publication_verdict.recommended_public_framing: stable intermediate baseline with bounded support/frontier packets
forbidden_framings: quantitative prediction without reproducible protocol/code/data/output hash/falsifier
publication_verdict.reason: All science blockers are terminal; owner/toolchain gates still control actual publication.

release_policy.release_unit: owner-review no-send baseline plus bounded support/frontier packets with all 82 release blockers terminal for 1.3.2
release_policy.not_a_release_unit: raw private feedback, raw model transcripts, unadjudicated theorem promotion, unsupported prediction wording
release_policy.claim_promotion_rule: support/frontier packets may create proof tasks, replay requirements and evidence-boundary records; they cannot promote canonical claims without proof/evidence gates
release_policy.why_1_3_2_is_built_this_way: It preserves the current stable OC Core baseline while exposing reviewed frontier material as bounded, no-send support; the 82 release blockers are terminal for 1.3.2 and external publication remains locked only by owner/channel actions.

science_inclusion_rows.claim_effect: evidence boundaries and reviewer-response routes preserved
domain lines are support/frontier material unless replay gates close
no Core promotion while refutation scope remains governed
claim-boundary corrections, proof tasks and replay requirements remain evidence-routed

science_backlog_rows.scientific_meaning: The canonical metamodel had tracked interface, level, domain and translation seams that required release-visible terminal support.
science_backlog_rows.terminal_closure: Closed for 1.3.2 by row-level proof/evidence, replay, theorem-fate discipline, or release-visible owner-gate evidence in the 82-row ledger.

science_backlog_rows.release_effect: Does not block 1.3.2 owner-review packaging; external publication still requires owner/channel unlock and must avoid inflated universal-completion framing.

science_backlog_rows.scientific_meaning: Root claim families for K0 substrate and K9 theory-construction required bounded proof/refutation support for the 1.3.2 release scope.
science_backlog_rows.terminal_closure: Closed for 1.3.2 by the root theorem stack, proof/refutation ledger, and claim-verdict evidence boundaries.
science_backlog_rows.future_work: Stronger TOE-level claims remain future work unless a later release supplies stronger proof support.
science_backlog_rows.release_effect: 1.3.2 may be framed as a bounded OC Core baseline, not as completed TOE proof.

science_backlog_rows.scientific_meaning: The proof/refutation discipline itself required a release-visible theorem-fate and counterexample-control route.
science_backlog_rows.terminal_closure: Closed for 1.3.2 by the verified theorem-fate ledger, claim verdict ledger, and refutation dossier.
science_backlog_rows.future_work: Additional theorem strengthening remains future work and cannot be implied by 1.3.2.
science_backlog_rows.release_effect: Keeps theorem language conservative and evidence-routed.

science_backlog_rows.scientific_meaning: Empirical and domain bridge rows required protocol/replay support or explicit structural-only classification.

science_backlog_rows.release_effect: Domain packets are release-supported bounded material, not unrestricted predictive authority.

science_backlog_rows.scientific_meaning: Publication and external-review actions must remain owner-gated even after science terminality.

science_backlog_rows.future_work: Owner approval, channel unlock, DOI/Zenodo/GitHub actions, and postflight verification are separate lawful actions.

science_backlog_rows.scientific_meaning: Value externalization must remain downstream of scientific and publication governance.
science_backlog_rows.terminal_closure: Closed as an owner-gated no-send terminal row with zero unapproved cash exposure and no outbound execution.
